title: "17 — XRF × compartment analysis (supplementary)"
subtitle: "Per-compartment breakdown of element → Shannon correlations"
format:
  html:
    toc: true
---

The per-element XRF–Shannon correlations reported in Fig. 1C of the
main paper are computed on site-mean Shannon (pooled across
compartments). This notebook asks a narrower question: do the salinity
(S, Cl, Na) and phosphorus effects operate uniformly across surface,
deep, and rhizosphere compartments, or is the signal compartment-specific?

For each of ten focal elements (S, Cl, Na, P, Fe, V, Mn, Ca, K, Si) and
each of three compartments (surface, deep, rhizosphere) we compute the
Spearman correlation of the element concentration with per-sample
Shannon diversity, and apply Benjamini–Hochberg FDR control across the
30 tests.

```{python}
#| label: setup
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
from pathlib import Path
from scipy import stats
from statsmodels.stats.multitest import multipletests
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

REPO = Path("..").resolve()
CACHE = REPO / "cache"
FIG = REPO / "figures"
FIG.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
```

```{python}
#| label: load
# per-sample Shannon from cached feature table
ft = pd.read_parquet(CACHE / "feature_table.parquet")
meta = pd.read_parquet(CACHE / "metadata.parquet")

def shannon(x):
    p = x[x > 0]
    p = p / p.sum()
    return float(-(p * np.log(p)).sum())

sh = ft.apply(shannon, axis=0).rename("Shannon")
sh.index.name = "sample"
meta_sh = meta.join(sh)
print(f"per-sample Shannon computed for {len(meta_sh)} samples")

# XRF table (158 samples, Trip 5 only)
xrf = pd.read_csv(REPO / "data/geochemistry/xrf_lab_table_filtered.tsv", sep="\t")
print(f"XRF table: {xrf.shape}")

# parse sample IDs: V<site><S|D|PR>r<rep>
pat = r"^V(\d+)(S|D|PR)r(\d+)$"
parsed = xrf["SampleID"].str.extract(pat)
xrf["site"] = pd.to_numeric(parsed[0], errors="coerce")
xrf["compartment"] = parsed[1].map({"S": "surface", "D": "deep", "PR": "rhizosphere"})
xrf["replicate"] = pd.to_numeric(parsed[2], errors="coerce")
print(f"XRF parsed: {xrf[['SampleID','site','compartment','replicate']].head(3)}")
print(f"compartment counts: {xrf.compartment.value_counts().to_dict()}")
```

```{python}
#| label: merge
# match XRF to Trip-5 Shannon per site × compartment
t5 = meta_sh[meta_sh["trip"] == 5].reset_index()
# XRF is one sample per (site, compartment); Trip 5 often has multiple replicates —
# average Shannon across replicates for the site × compartment match
t5_mean = t5.groupby(["site", "compartment"])["Shannon"].mean().reset_index()

merged = xrf.merge(t5_mean, on=["site", "compartment"], how="inner")
print(f"merged XRF × Shannon per (site, compartment): {merged.shape}")
print(f"per-compartment counts: {merged.compartment.value_counts().to_dict()}")
```

```{python}
#| label: correlate
ELEMENTS = ["S", "Cl", "Na", "P", "Fe", "V", "Mn", "Ca", "K", "Si"]
COMPARTMENTS = ["surface", "deep", "rhizosphere"]

rows = []
for elem in ELEMENTS:
    if elem not in merged.columns:
        print(f"  SKIP {elem} — not in XRF table")
        continue
    for comp in COMPARTMENTS:
        sub = merged[merged.compartment == comp].dropna(subset=[elem, "Shannon"])
        if len(sub) < 8:
            rows.append({"element": elem, "compartment": comp, "rho": np.nan,
                         "p": np.nan, "n": len(sub)})
            continue
        rho, p = stats.spearmanr(sub[elem], sub["Shannon"])
        rows.append({"element": elem, "compartment": comp, "rho": rho,
                     "p": p, "n": len(sub)})

res = pd.DataFrame(rows)
valid = res.dropna(subset=["p"])
_, q, _, _ = multipletests(valid["p"].values, method="fdr_bh")
res.loc[valid.index, "q"] = q
res["significant"] = res["q"] < 0.05
res.to_csv(CACHE / "xrf_per_compartment.tsv", sep="\t", index=False)
print(res.to_string(index=False))
```

```{python}
#| label: fig-s30
#| fig-cap: "Per-compartment XRF × Shannon Spearman correlations."
pivot_rho = res.pivot(index="element", columns="compartment", values="rho").reindex(ELEMENTS)[COMPARTMENTS]
pivot_q = res.pivot(index="element", columns="compartment", values="q").reindex(ELEMENTS)[COMPARTMENTS]

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(4.5, 5.2))
vmax = np.nanmax(np.abs(pivot_rho.values))
im = ax.imshow(pivot_rho.values, cmap="RdBu_r", vmin=-vmax, vmax=vmax, aspect="auto")

for i, elem in enumerate(ELEMENTS):
    for j, comp in enumerate(COMPARTMENTS):
        rho = pivot_rho.iloc[i, j]
        q = pivot_q.iloc[i, j]
        if not np.isnan(rho):
            mark = ""
            if not np.isnan(q):
                if q < 0.001: mark = "***"
                elif q < 0.01: mark = "**"
                elif q < 0.05: mark = "*"
            ax.text(j, i, f"{rho:+.2f}{mark}", ha="center", va="center",
                    fontsize=8, color="white" if abs(rho) > 0.35 else "black")

ax.set_xticks(range(len(COMPARTMENTS)))
ax.set_xticklabels([c[:4] for c in COMPARTMENTS])
ax.set_yticks(range(len(ELEMENTS)))
ax.set_yticklabels(ELEMENTS)
ax.set_xlabel("Compartment")
ax.set_ylabel("Element")
ax.set_title("XRF × Shannon (per compartment)\nSpearman ρ (BH-FDR q <0.05 marked *)", fontsize=9)
cb = plt.colorbar(im, ax=ax, shrink=0.7)
cb.set_label("Spearman ρ")
fig.tight_layout()
fig.savefig(FIG / "figS30_xrf_per_compartment.pdf", bbox_inches="tight")
plt.show()
```

## Interpretation

After BH-FDR correction across the 30 element × compartment tests,
**two associations survive at q < 0.05**, both in the rhizosphere
compartment:

- **Sulfur → Shannon (rhizosphere):** ρ = -0.44, q = 0.016 (n = 53).
- **Chloride → Shannon (rhizosphere):** ρ = -0.44, q = 0.016 (n = 53).

The salinity suite is therefore **compartment-specific** rather than
uniform:

- **S / Cl** act most strongly where roots are present, consistent
  with host-plant filtering: saline rhizospheres recruit a narrower
  pool of salt-tolerant associates, collapsing community evenness.
  The signal is directionally consistent but not significant in
  surface / deep.
- **Na** shows the opposite compartmental pattern — strongest in
  surface (ρ = -0.57, raw p = 0.006, q = 0.059 after FDR) and deep
  (ρ = -0.34), near zero in rhizosphere. Surface sodium concentrates
  at evaporitic crusts; rhizospheres appear to decouple Na
  concentration from community diversity.
- **P** flips sign across compartments: positive in deep (ρ = +0.35,
  raw p = 0.04) and negative in rhizosphere (ρ = -0.36, raw p = 0.009,
  q = 0.066 marginal). The site-mean phosphorus signal reported in
  main Fig. 1C (ρ = +0.34) therefore masks a compartment-specific
  sign flip.
- **Ca** is the other strong candidate: negative in surface (ρ =
  -0.40) and deep (ρ = -0.41, marginal q = 0.09), consistent with a
  carbonate/evaporite effect in bulk soils, and near zero in the
  rhizosphere.
- **Fe, V, Mn, K, Si** show no per-compartment associations that
  survive FDR correction.

**Takeaway for the main paper.** The overall salinity→Shannon story
is robust, but its mechanism is compartment-specific: sulfur and
chloride act on roots, while sodium acts in bulk surface soil. The
phosphorus sign flip (deep +, rhiz −) suggests that the main-text
Spearman ρ = +0.34 for site-mean P reflects predominantly deep/surface
oasis-sample points and does not extend uniformly to the rhizosphere
compartment. These compartment-specific patterns are not contradicted
by the main-text analyses but add resolution that the site-mean
treatment obscures.

The full 10 × 3 table with n, raw p, and BH-FDR q values is saved to
`cache/xrf_per_compartment.tsv`; the figure is
`figS30_xrf_per_compartment.pdf`.
